'''Ruth Jeannette Williams''' is an Australian-born American mathematician at the [[University of California, San Diego]] where she holds the Charles Lee Powell Chair as a Distinguished Professor of Mathematics. Her research concerns [[probability theory]] and [[stochastic process]]es.<ref>[http://www.math.ucsd.edu/~williams/ Ruth Williams], UCSD, retrieved 2014-12-24.</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Williams was born in Australia and moved to the United States in 1978.<ref name=":1" />

Williams graduated from the [[University of Melbourne]] with a Bachelor of Sciences, with honors, in 1976 and a Master of Science in mathematics in 1978.<ref>{{citation|url=https://ms.unimelb.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0010/2942569/Citation-Ruth-Williams-UPDATED-new.pdf|title=Citation in support of Ruth Williams' nomination for an Honorary Doctorate|date=December 11, 2018|website=University of Melbourne|access-date=November 23, 2019}}</ref>  Williams went on to earn her Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1983, under the supervision of [[Chung Kai-lai]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Ruth Jeannette Williams|id=22520}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/1065286|title=Brownian motion in a wedge with oblique reflection at the boundary /|last=Williams|first=Ruth Jeannette|publisher=Stanford University|year=1983}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
Williams was president of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] from 2011 to 2012.

Williams is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and a [[fellow]] of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[American Mathematical Society]], the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]],<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20111206195340/http://www.math.ucsd.edu/people/faculty/Ruth-Williams/ Faculty profile], UCSD, retrieved 2014-12-24.</ref> and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2020-fellows|title=SIAM Announces Class of 2020 Fellows|work=SIAM News |publisher=SIAM|date=March 31, 2020|access-date=2020-06-12}}</ref> In 1998 she was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{citation|author=Williams, Ruth J.|chapter=Reflecting diffusions and queueing networks|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. III|year=1998|pages=321–330|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011589000}}</ref> Williams was an [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Council member at large.<ref>{{citation |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

Her other awards and honors include:
* Alfred P. Sloan Fellow (1988) <ref>{{citation|url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows|title=Past Fellows|website=sloan.org|access-date=2019-11-23}}</ref>
* Guggenheim Fellow (2001)<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/ruth-j-williams/|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{!}} Ruth J. Williams|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-23}}</ref>
* Best Publication Award of the INFORMS Applied Probability Society (2007), jointly with [[Amber L. Puha]] and [[H. Christian Gromoll]]<ref name=":0">{{citation|url=https://acems.org.au/our-people/ruth-williams|title=Ruth Williams {{!}} ARC Centre of Excellence for Mathematical and Statistical Frontiers|website=acems.org.au|access-date=2019-11-23}}</ref>
*[[John von Neumann Theory Prize]] (2016), jointly with [[Martin I. Reiman]] for "seminal research contributions over the past several decades, to the theory and applications of stochastic networks/systems and their heavy traffic approximations".<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.informs.org/ORMS-Today/Public-Articles/December-Volume-43-Number-6/INFORMS-News-Reiman-Williams-share-von-Neumann-Prize|title=Reiman, Williams share von Neumann Prize|journal=INFORMS News|publisher=[[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]]|volume=43|issue=6|date=December 2016}}</ref>
*Honorary Doctorate from the University of Melbourne (2018) <ref name=":1">{{citation|url=https://ms.unimelb.edu.au/news/ruth-williams-recieves-honorary-doctorate|title=Ruth Williams receives Honorary Doctorate|last=Cashin|first=Kasey|date=2018-12-11|website=School of Mathematics and Statistics|language=en|access-date=2019-11-23}}</ref>
* [[WORMS Award|Award for the Advancement of Women in Operations Research and the Management Sciences]] (2017), annual INFORMS meeting<ref name=":0" />
* Honorary Doctor of Science degree from La Trobe University in Australia<ref name=":0" />
* National Science Foundation Presidential Young Investigator<ref name=":0" />
